# Artifact Keeper 1.11.0

A large release: roughly 210 changelog entries across about 170 merged pull requests since 1.10.0. The headline additions are hosted Arch Linux (pacman) and Bazel module repositories (#3343, #2858), a third repository visibility, `internal` (#3812), lifecycle policies that can be assigned to chosen repositories, combine conditions and reclaim a Remote's proxy cache (#3794, #4456, #3734), scan-on-proxy for Maven, Gradle, sbt, NuGet and Cargo (#4100, #4102, #4101), Ed25519-signed webhooks verifiable against a public JWKS (#4401), and distributed tracing that follows a request from the caller through the proxy to the upstream and the database (#4029, #4434, #4455). The rest is mostly security and correctness work on proxies, virtual repositories, formats and storage. This page groups the highlights; the `## [1.11.0]` section of `CHANGELOG.md` has every entry.

1.11.0 also contains every fix shipped in 1.10.1 and 1.10.2, listed again under their sections below as 1.10.0 did for 1.9.1. If you are upgrading from 1.10.2, the token-scoping, webhook-read, OSV-scanning and wasmtime entries are already deployed.

**Upgrading runs 35 migrations** (222 to 269, excluding the numbers that were never used and 235 and 237, which shipped in 1.10.2). One of them, **233, requires stopping every old backend replica before it runs**; see the first section. Two are backfills over existing rows; see "Operations and migrations". <!-- TODO(W5/W6): add 270/271 (#4153/#4463 origin re-stamp and credential strip), 272 (#4424 pacman file lists) and 273 (#4425/#4426) if they land, and update the count. -->

## Read this first: stop all replicas before migration 233

**Lifecycle policies are now scoped by explicit repository assignments, and an older binary misreads the new scope as "every repository"** (#3794, migration 233). A policy now carries `applies_to_all` plus a list of assigned repositories. Older binaries treat any policy that has no single `repository_id` as global, and after the migration that includes every unassigned policy and every policy assigned to two or more repositories. An old replica or lifecycle scheduler still running while 233 is applied could therefore delete artifacts across the whole instance.

- **Scale the backend to zero (or otherwise stop every old pod and scheduler) before upgrading. Do not do a rolling or mixed-version deploy.** Helm upgrades are rolling by default.
- Downgrading to 1.10.x after 233 is unsafe unless policy scopes are first reconciled by hand.
- Two API changes come with it. Creating a policy without `repository_id` now creates a dormant policy that deletes nothing, not a global one: CLI, Terraform and other clients that relied on the old default must send `applies_to_all: true`. Deleting a repository no longer deletes its single-repository policies; it removes the assignment and leaves the policy dormant.

The migration itself preserves behaviour: a policy with a null `repository_id` becomes `applies_to_all = true`, and a single-repository policy gets one assignment.

## Read this second: requests that are now refused

- **Hex publish without a usable `CHECKSUM` member answers `422`** (#2904). Such a tarball used to be stored and then made every `/packages/{name}` read answer 500. `mix hex.build` always writes the member, so only hand-built tarballs are affected.
- **`POST /api/v1/signing/keys` with `key_type = ed25519` answers `400`** (#1326). That combination never produced an Ed25519 key: it stored an RSA keypair labelled `ed25519`, which could not sign Debian or RPM metadata. Ask for `key_type = gpg` with `algorithm = ed25519`, which now generates a real v4 EdDSA OpenPGP key. Existing `ed25519` rows keep loading.
- **Creating or updating a repository as public while guest access is disabled answers `400`** (#3855) instead of silently storing it as private. Terraform and other clients that send `is_public: true` on a guest-disabled instance must stop doing so.
- **A lifecycle policy that cannot reclaim anything in a Remote repository answers `422` when it is assigned there** (#3734): `max_versions`, `tag_pattern_*`, `size_quota_bytes`, `exclude` lists and `min_keep` match artifact versions that proxy-cache entries do not have. OCI Remotes are exempt. Policies already assigned keep running.
- **Scan-on-proxy now enforces for Maven, Gradle, sbt, NuGet, Chocolatey, PowerShell and Cargo Remotes that already had it enabled** (#4100, #4102, #4101), and for the VS Code legacy download route (#4098). A vulnerable package answers `403 scan_blocked`, and under `fail_closed` an unscannable one answers `423`. These pulls were served unscanned before, so gates that were never exercised can start blocking. `GET /api/v1/formats` reports which formats enforce (#4099); `docs/security/scan-on-proxy.md` has the matrix (#4114). <!-- TODO(W5): #4442 adds the generic `/download/*path` route to the gate for Remote Maven and NuGet; mention it here once merged. -->
- **Known-malicious packages are graded `Critical`** (#3013). OSV `MAL-*` advisories usually carry no severity and used to default to `Medium`, below a typical `max_severity = high` gate. They are now classed `malicious` and graded `Critical`, so a gate can start blocking packages it used to pass.
- **A multipart publish over `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE` answers `413`, not `400`** (#3936), and **completing a chunked upload onto an occupied immutable path answers `409`** instead of replacing the artifact (#3924).
<!-- TODO(W5): #4461 lifecycle regexes are PostgreSQL dialect and `\b` is refused (422); #4419 webhook event names are validated; #4161 `origin.allowed_kinds: proxy` is refused. Add one bullet each once merged. -->

## Read this third: behaviour that changes without an error

- **Docker Hub credentials need a trusted token realm** (#3591). Since GHSA-78h6-3wp8-2542 a Remote only sends its upstream credentials to a Bearer realm on the upstream's own origin, and Docker Hub issues tokens from `auth.docker.io`. The new per-Remote `oci_trusted_bearer_realms` list names the extra origins that may receive them. Nothing is trusted by default, Docker Hub included: **a credentialed Docker Hub Remote must add `"oci_trusted_bearer_realms": ["https://auth.docker.io"]`** to pull private images or use its account rate limits. Without it, pulls fall back to anonymous tokens. Split-host GitLab registries need the same. See `docs/oci-trusted-bearer-realms.md`.
- **Lifecycle policies reclaim a Remote's proxy cache only when explicitly assigned to that Remote** (#3734). `max_age_days` and `no_downloads_days` now evict proxy-cache entries, but global (`applies_to_all`) policies never reach a Remote cache, which may hold the only copy of content that is gone upstream. A global run says so in `proxy_cache.skipped_reason`. Run a preview before assigning one: `max_age_days` evicts by cache age, however often an entry is used.
- **Cache TTLs: higher ceiling, and lowering one takes effect at once** (#2667, #3832). The per-Remote TTL override can now go up to ten years (315360000 seconds), which stops revalidation of mutable paths. Lowering a TTL now applies to entries already cached instead of waiting out each entry's original expiry, and a `304` revalidation refreshes `cached_at`. The web UI's TTL input still has the old maximum (artifact-keeper-web).
- **`AK_GUEST_ACCESS_ENABLED`, when set, overrides the new runtime toggle** (#867). Guest access can now be switched at runtime through `PATCH /api/v1/admin/settings/system`. An explicit `true`/`false`/`1`/`0` in the environment still wins, as an offline break-glass. To hand an instance that runs with `false` over to the admin setting without reopening anonymous access, `PATCH` `false` first, then remove the variable.
- **Webhooks v2** (#4401). A webhook's new `signing_mode` (`hmac`, the default; `asymmetric`; `both`) adds a `v2=<kid>:<sig>` Ed25519 signature verifiable against `GET /api/v1/webhooks/jwks`. Existing webhooks stay `hmac` and their headers are byte-identical. `asymmetric` and `both` need `AK_WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY` set; if that key changes after the signing key exists, asymmetric deliveries go out without `v2=` until an administrator retires the key by hand (the SQL is in the CHANGELOG entry). Key rotation follows in a later release.
- **`ak_http_request_duration_seconds` is a histogram now, so its `quantile` series are gone** (#4434). Panels and alerts that select `{quantile="0.99"}` must use `histogram_quantile()` over the `_bucket` series, which also makes the percentile aggregatable across replicas. Each label set exports 16 series instead of 9.
- **An OCI image deleted by digest stays deleted after a restart** (#4450), with one gap (#4465). An image pushed only by tag (for example by `skopeo copy --all`) and deleted by digest on an older release, or by a not-yet-upgraded replica during the rollout, can still come back on the first restart after the upgrade. **After every replica runs 1.11.0, check images deleted by digest before and during the rollout, and delete them again.** <!-- TODO: drop this caveat if #4465 lands before the cut. -->
- **Upstream credentials embedded in `upstream_url` are no longer returned by the API** (#4452), but copies already stored are not removed. Rotate any secret that was embedded in a Remote's URL and move it to the encrypted upstream-auth fields. <!-- TODO(W5): #4463 strips the stored copies (migration 271); reword once merged. -->
- **The bundles API is a preview** (#4400, #2464): it describes and validates the bundle format, but `POST /api/v1/bundles/exports` and `/imports` answer `501` until the export and import steps land. **Remote and virtual pacman repositories are not supported yet** (#4407).
<!-- TODO(W5): #4417 presigned redirects need S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT when clients reach the object store through a different host than the backend. -->

## Security

- **Tokens and access control.** A personal token created with a `repo_selector` is confined to it (#4219); a repository-restricted token can no longer mint an unrestricted one (#4225); a restriction no longer fails open on an unreadable selector or a misspelled field (#4226); a token whose repositories were all deleted no longer becomes unrestricted (#4228); webhook fetch-by-id needs the same grant as the listing (#3901). All five shipped in 1.10.2. Artifact label writes need the repository `write` action (#4193), bulk promotion applies the quality gate and the CVE and licence policy per item (#3979), the OCI `/v2/token` exchange is rate limited like `/api/v1/auth/login` (#4020), and the CI OIDC exchange no longer merges principals across issuers or reactivates a deactivated account (#4032).
- **Leaks.** Upstream credentials embedded in `upstream_url` are redacted from every API response, audit record and log line that carried them (#4452). LDAP login no longer reveals through its timing whether a username exists (#3505), and the detailed health payload no longer echoes the raw storage error (#3907).
- **Content that should not have been served.** npm and Maven virtual repositories no longer serve a hosted member's artifact that the member's scan policy blocks (#4286), RPM virtual repodata lists only the members the caller may read (#4346), and the VS Code legacy download route is scan-gated (#4098).
- **Tracing input.** Inbound W3C trace context is adopted only from peers inside `RATE_LIMIT_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` once that list is set, so a client can no longer force or suppress sampling (#4195).
- **Dependencies.** wasmtime 36.0.16 (#4332, shipped in 1.10.2) and 36.0.17 (#4361) for RUSTSEC-2026-0314, -0316, -0321, -0322 and -0323 in the WASM plugin runtime. CEP-27 conda attestations are now verified when `CONDA_ATTESTATION_REQUIRE_VERIFIED` is set (#4155).
<!-- TODO(W5): #4418 (promotion authz), #4420 (SSRF on DNS rebinding), #4442 (generic route scan gate). -->

## Proxy and virtual repositories

- **Filters and isolation.** A Remote can restrict which paths it requests upstream with include and exclude patterns, and a virtual no longer waits on a member whose filter excludes the path (#4399). npm virtual repositories can isolate hosted package names from upstream (#3767). Docker Hub and split-host registries can authenticate through trusted realms (#3591).
- **Caching.** TTL ceiling and immediate TTL lowering (#2667, #3832); Go module versions are cached instead of revalidated every five minutes (#4120); GitHub release-by-tag lookups are cached for seven days (#3658); a request arriving during a refill no longer duplicates the upstream fetch (#4298); remote Debian pool downloads no longer list the whole proxy cache (#4315).
- **Virtual correctness.** Nested virtual members resolve (#3840); npm virtuals no longer fail `npm install` with EINTEGRITY when a hosted member shadows a remote one (#3955) and walk members concurrently (#4240); Cargo virtuals use each member's own download template (#3952) and shadow only the exact local `name@version` (#3953); NuGet serves both protocol surfaces across all members (#4126).
- **Scan-on-proxy.** New enforcement for Maven, Gradle, sbt, NuGet and Cargo (#4100, #4102, #4101); a `record_only` action that records findings without blocking pulls (#3645); quarantine holds stop virtual walks (#4098).
<!-- TODO(W5/W6): #4365 canonical proxy paths, #3844 proxy download statistics, #4013 single-flight layering. -->

## Formats

- **New.** Hosted pacman repositories with on-demand `.db`/`.files` and detached signatures (#3343); Bazel module registry (Bzlmod) repositories (#2858); GitHub release mirroring through `github`, `mise` and `aqua` formats (#3656); a hosted VS Code repository served through the gallery protocol, and virtual galleries (#3959, #3962).
- **Signing.** Ed25519 OpenPGP keys (#1326), an overlap window in which both the old and the new key sign Debian and RPM metadata after a rotation (#1329), and a startup warning, with optional automatic replacement, for keys that cannot sign the metadata they are bound to (#1331).
- **RPM, Maven, Debian and others.** Hosted RPM repositories publish dependency metadata (#3801), serve metadata at a configured directory depth (#4216) and can prune curated snapshots (#4406). Maven: uploads commit atomically (#3587), `.meta/prefixes.txt` no longer breaks Maven 4 (#4367) and virtual downloads count (#4267). `.safetensors` uploads expose tensor structure (#4402); chunked uploads of Incus images and Debian packages get native metadata (#4403); RubyGems remote specs no longer come back empty (#4280); Conan v2 answers 404 for missing items (#3887).
- **Conda.** The content-analysis work (#4033 and follow-ups) identifies what is inside a package, maps conda dependencies to PyPI advisories (#4042, #4089), records provenance and publisher identity (#4049, #4050), and can withdraw a single package with a CEP-6 notice (#4059).
<!-- TODO(W6): #4424 pacman file lists (migration 272), #4466/#4449/#4453 OCI fixes. -->

## Lifecycle, storage and uploads

- **Lifecycle.** Explicit assignment (#3794), composite conditions and tag or version patterns (#4456), newest-N retention under an age rule and path-prefix scope (#2024), and proxy-cache reclamation for Remotes (#3734).
- **Trash and repair.** `GC_TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS` keeps soft-deleted artifacts restorable by an admin for that many days; the default `0` keeps today's behaviour (#2072). Storage scrub detects, and from a verified copy repairs, corrupt content-addressed objects (#3910). Admins can register artifacts that exist in storage with no database row (#1570).
- **Object storage.** Raw `PUT` and multipart uploads into S3, GCS and Azure no longer spool to local disk (#3916, #4404); OCI blob pulls can be served by a presigned-URL redirect (#2894); quality checks read the repository's configured backend (#3736); chunked uploads work behind several replicas (#3918) and clean up after themselves (#3922).
- **Projects.** Project admins manage their own membership and repositories (#2473), and project storage quotas are enforced across the project's repositories (#2474).
<!-- TODO(W5): #4417 presigned public endpoint. -->

## Observability

The backend joins the caller's trace (#4029), adopts it only from trusted proxies once configured (#4195), and its sampler is configurable through `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` (#4029). Upstream requests are `CLIENT` spans that carry the trace onward (#4434, #4455), the request span records the route, status, repository and cache outcome, and authentication, virtual-resolution and proxy-fetch phases appear as their own spans (#4455). With export configured, SQL statements can appear as `CLIENT` spans; SQL text is never exported (#4455). Request-scoped stdout log lines now show these spans too. `ak_http_request_duration_seconds` is a Prometheus histogram instead of a summary (#4434; see the third section). OTLP `http/protobuf` export works (#3833), and the gRPC and metrics listeners can bind a specific IP (#2161).

## Operations and migrations

**35 migrations** run on start-up (222 to 234, 236, 238 to 269 as present on disk). Most are additive. The ones to plan for:

- **233** (#3794) needs every old replica stopped first; see the first section.
- **228** backfills `artifacts.origin` for existing rows in resumable batches outside a transaction (#4050). It runs once, on the upgrade that applies it, and its time grows with the number of artifacts.
- **268** creates the `oci_manifests` table (#4433); a background task started at boot then records manifests pushed before the upgrade, reading each body from storage. Nothing reads the table yet in 1.11.0, so the backfill is not on any request path. A 1.10.x replica writes no row for its pushes, which is one more reason to stop every old replica before upgrading (migration 233 requires it anyway); reconciling the table is part of the later release that starts reading it.
- **227 to 231** add the origin column, its trigger, validation and index; 229 and 230 build their indexes `CONCURRENTLY`.
<!-- TODO: start-up time of 228 and 268 measured on the v1.10.2 snapshot rehearsal (delivery plan checklist). TODO(W5): 270/271 relax and re-enable the 227 immutability trigger. -->

Other operator-facing additions: maintenance and downtime banners (#2155), the guest-access runtime toggle (#867), `BLOB_GC_MIN_AGE_SECS` (#2906), LDAP group and admin re-sync on a schedule with optional deactivation (#3830), permission rules restricted by request CIDR, including anonymous read grants (#1849), and the scanner-adapter's client mode against a shared `trivy server` (#4351, adapter 1.4.0). The runtime images now ship `unsquashfs` for Incus SquashFS scans (#4469). Release runs now dispatch the release announcement and the AMI build themselves (#3896, #3897).

## Other repositories

- **artifact-keeper-web:** TTL input maximum of ten years, Ed25519 key-type select, guest-access toggle and banners admin pages, project-admin membership, lifecycle assignment and composite policies, `internal` visibility, webhook `signing_mode`, and the new search and artifact fields (`last_promotion`, `format_key`, quarantine state). Regenerate the SDK from the 1.11.0 spec.
- **artifact-keeper-iac (Helm chart):** values for the new settings (`GRPC_BIND_IP`, `METRICS_BIND_IP`, `BLOB_GC_MIN_AGE_SECS`, `GC_TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS`, `LDAP_SYNC_*`, `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER[_ARG]`, `SIGNING_KEY_ROTATION_OVERLAP_SECS`, `SIGNING_AUTO_MIGRATE_LEGACY_KEYS`, `CONDA_ATTESTATION_REQUIRE_VERIFIED`, `STORAGE_SCRUB_*`, the scanner-adapter `SCANNER_TRIVY_SERVER`), scanner-adapter tag 1.4.0, and a note that the backend must be scaled to zero for this upgrade (migration 233). The chart must not set `AK_GUEST_ACCESS_ENABLED`, which now pins the runtime toggle.
- **artifact-keeper-cli:** lifecycle commands must send `applies_to_all: true` for a global policy (#3794).
- **artifact-keeper-api:** the 1.11.0 OpenAPI spec and SDK regeneration.
